title: Label every image for what it is
statement: Label every image truthfully: a real photograph or painting with its credit and what it really shows, never as a story's own place, and an invented illustration as an illustration.
detail: A unit film's design required an honest credit and location label for each image, with no real garden photograph labelled as the novel's house and no historical painting implied to depict the story; the produced film printed the painting's credit and showed it as a regional scene, explicitly not the fictional manor. A source audit of another grade found an illustration captioned as if it were a real ancient object, with no object, collection or edition provenance, and asked that passage images be labelled and assessed as authored illustrations. The book-style paintings added later record their settings as invented, not claims about a real location or a historic theatre.

evidence.quote: Each image needs an honest credit and location label. Do not label a photographed real garden as Misselthwaite or imply the historical painting depicts the story.
Credit printed on video. Regional scene, explicitly not the fictional manor.
Scroll caption presents an illustrative reconstruction as “like this one”; no object, collection or edition provenance.
Passage images may be useful authored illustrations; label and assess them as such, especially when they introduce content used by the lesson.
Manor geography and theatre architecture are invented settings, not claims about the exact novel location or historic Globe.
